text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Farmers affected by floods will get fresh credits even if they failed to pay back old ones, the paper says.
- President Emil Constantinescu promulgated the bill giving foreigners the right to own land to set up businesses in Romania.
- The Bucharest commodities exchange plans to sell old rolling stock in a tender.
- Unipetrol of the Czech Republic is interested in the privatisation of Romania's refineries.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The private airline Dac Air will inaugurate flights to Cluj starting April 28.
- The government is expected to issue a programme for the restructuring and privatisation of the machine building sector, the paper says.
- The government included the Romanian ocean fishing company on the list of loss-making firms earmarked for closure, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian motorists plan to protest against new tax road imposed by the transport ministry in order to create a fund to finance repairs needed by the infrastructure.
ADEVARUL
- Number of loss-making companies earmarked for closure amounts now to 36, the paper quotes industry ministry data as saying.
- Floods affected seven counties across Romania, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Some 60 opposition deputies contested a recent bank privatisation law, saying it breaches the constitutional principle of equal access to privatisation.
- Prosecutors started investigations in the case of businessman George Danielescu, head of the SAFI Invest administrator of the troubled FMOA unit trust, on allegations of forgery and fraud.

- Journalist Octavian Andronic, director of the daily Libertatea, was stabbed and beaten by two armed burglars on Tuesday. Police arrested two suspects for attempted murder, armed robbery and breaking and entering.
- Armed robbery in Romania is on the rise, President Emil Constantinescu said.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright told Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin that NATO expansion will not end at the alliance's Madrid summit, the newspaper says. It says the phrase was a diplomatic way of telling Romania that it would not be in among first wave entrants.

- Seven Romanian ships were seized in various ports across the world after their owner Self Invest Maritime failed to pay debts and abandoned them, the newspaper says. Some 70 Romanian sailors are treated like slaves on these ships.
ADEVARUL
- Leading businessman George Constantin Paunescu used a $10 million credit from Chase Manhattan Bank to buy a share in private Bankcoop bank, his lawyer said.

- Romania does not want to be left out NATO's first wave of expansion only "to be used as an instrument for encouraging Eastern European states which do not qualify for early entrance", Severin told the newspaper.
- President Constantinescu made public his expenditures of 800 million lei, made during the 1996 election campaign.
($ = 7,072 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
